title: Testing segment of the round
statement: Let $C,D$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet with positive numbers of work tapes, choose states $c_e,c_x$ of $C$ and $d_e,d_x$ of $D$, and let $w,s,u,v$ be Boolean words. Suppose $a,b>0$; from its seam on input $w$ with $s$ on its first tape, $C$ avoids $c_x$ at all times strictly between $0$ and $a$ and reaches $c_x$ at time $a$ with $u$ on its first tape. From its seam on input $w$ with the suffix of $w$ after its first $|s|$ bits on its first tape, $D$ avoids $d_x$ strictly between $0$ and $b$ and reaches $d_x$ at time $b$ with $v$ on its first tape. Then, starting from the completed-preparation configuration with $s$ on the candidate and width tapes and that suffix on the length tape, the controller reaches, at some time $t\le a+b+2(\max(|u|,|v|)+1)+4$, the first erasure phase with verdict equal to whether $u=v$, preserving those words on their respective tapes; no configuration from time $0$ through time $t$ has the anchor state.
hypotheses_covered: C and D are finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machines
C and D each have a positive number of work tapes
ce and cx are states of C
de and dx are states of D
w, s, u, and v are Boolean words
a and b are positive natural numbers
C avoids cx at all times strictly between 0 and a from its stated seam configuration
C is at cx with first tape containing u at time a
D avoids dx at all times strictly between 0 and b from its stated seam configuration
D is at dx with first tape containing v at time b
replaced:
Suppose the width call completes in $a > 0$ steps with result $u$ and the
suffix-length call completes in $b > 0$ steps with result $v$, each with no
interior exit-state visit. Then there is a time
$t \le a + b + 2(\max(\abs{u},\abs{v}) + 1) + 4$ after which the
controller, from its completed-preparation seam, has run both calls and the
whole-word comparison and sits at the first erasure seam carrying the
verdict of $u = v$; both calls are charged before any relation between
their results is assumed, and the trace avoids the anchor.
